content: Bisocotrizole, also known by its USAN name and marketed under the trade name Tinosorb® M, is a chemical compound with the INCI designation Methylene Bis-Benzotriazolyl Tetramethylbutylphenol. It is incorporated into sunscreen formulations to effectively absorb ultraviolet (UV) radiation. This compound is produced and distributed by Ciba Specialty Chemicals. Bisocotrizole functions as a broad-spectrum UV radiation absorber, capable of absorbing both UVB and UVA rays. Additionally, it has the ability to reflect and scatter UV radiation, enhancing its protective properties. It is classified as a hybrid UV absorber, combining characteristics of both organic and inorganic sunscreen agents. The compound is manufactured in the form of small particles, typically less than 200 nanometers in size, similar to microfine zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. Despite its particle size, it is considered an organic compound, akin to most active ingredients in sunscreens. In sunscreen formulations, bisocotrizole is introduced into the water phase as a 50% suspension, in contrast to mineral micropigments, which are generally added to the oil phase. One of its notable properties is its high photostability, meaning it undergoes minimal photodegradation when exposed to sunlight. Furthermore, bisocotrizole has a stabilizing effect on other UV absorbers, particularly octyl methoxycinnamate (commonly known as octinoxate), enhancing their performance and longevity. Unlike certain other organic sunscreen agents, bisocotrizole does not exhibit estrogenic effects in vitro, making it a safer option in this regard. However, it is important to note that bisocotrizole has not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in sunscreens. Nevertheless, it has received regulatory approval in the European Union and various other regions worldwide.
